neighbours.label: the slot right before 'unaware / don't know / never notice': people who have or pass something without knowing it
fire: Nearly a third of adults have prediabetes, and most are unaware of their condition.
Thousands of drivers carry a faulty airbag and simply do not realise it.
One in five people with hepatitis B remain undiagnosed for decades.
Tourists stroll past the buried city every day and never suspect it is there.
An estimated million households have radon in the basement but have no idea.
Many carriers of the gene show no symptoms and never learn they have it.
Shoppers hand over their data at the till, often without knowing it.
Plenty of homeowners live on a fault line and are oblivious to the risk.
quiet: Nearly a third of adults have prediabetes, and most are treated with diet changes.
Thousands of drivers carry a faulty airbag and have booked a free repair.
One in five people with hepatitis B are given antiviral tablets each year.
Tourists stroll past the buried city every day on the way to the beach.
An estimated million households have radon in the basement and have fitted fans.
Many carriers of the gene take part in yearly screening at the clinic.
Shoppers hand over their loyalty cards at the till to collect points.
Plenty of homeowners live on a fault line and have earthquake insurance.
